newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Tajik government vows to halt rebel advance.
newsitem.headline: Tajik government vows to halt rebel advance.

text.p: U.N. military observers in Tajikistan said on Monday that fighting around the disputed town of Garm had died down but the embattled Tajik government vowed to check any further advances by Islamist guerrillas.
"Garm is quiet and there are now talks," an officer with the United Nations' Mission of Observers to Tajikistan (UNMOT) told Reuters on condition of anonymity. He gave no further details.
Islamist guerrillas said they had seized the town situated 200 km (130 miles) east of the capital Dushanbe on Sunday.
The flare-up in fighting in the former Soviet republic came only days before planned peace talks between Tajik President Imomali Rakhmonov and opposition leader Sayid Abdullo Nuri on December 9.
A senior Tajik official said the government would take "adequate measures" to repulse any continued opposition attacks.

Cited by Russia's Interfax news agency, Rakhmonov's defence adviser, Mizrob Kabirov, said the measures would be used "to prevent the negative development of events and to stop any escalation in military action on Tajik territory".

Tajik government troops and Islamist guerrillas have fought a bitter civil war for nearly five years, leaving tens of thousands dead and many more homeless among the remote, mountainous country's 5.7 million population.
